business_problem: Dadi Quantum needed to turn PB-scale satellite, drone, and sensor data into precise weather and renewable-power forecasts, but training end-to-end AI meteorology models and serving a cloud-native spatial data platform required burst GPU compute, high-throughput shared storage, and low-cost long-term retention that a growing company could not provision efficiently on its own.
solution_summary: Dadi Quantum built its AI remote-sensing stack on Alibaba Cloud so it could convert satellite, drone, and sensor data into weather and renewable-power forecasting services without carrying fixed infrastructure sized for peak training runs. Multi-source spatial data from NASA, the European Space Agency, and other providers is ingested into the company's cloud-native spatiotemporal PaaS, where proprietary algorithms grid, index, and organize the data pool for downstream model development and SDK access. On top of that data layer, Dadi Quantum trains end-to-end AI meteorology models for short-term weather prediction and site-level power forecasting, using Alibaba Cloud GPU instances for burst compute, CPFS for high-throughput low-latency training reads, and OSS for tiered long-term storage of massive historical datasets. Forecast outputs then feed renewable-energy planning, dispatch, and trading scenarios through the platform's SDK and application services.

solution_components.name: cloud-native spatiotemporal PaaS
solution_components.role: Provides the grid-managed spatial data platform that organizes multi-source remote-sensing data and exposes reusable services.

solution_components.name: SDK
solution_components.role: Gives customers and application teams programmatic access to Dadi Quantum's spatial-data and forecasting services.

solution_components.name: AI meteorology model
solution_components.role: Generates short-term weather forecasts and renewable-power predictions from fused remote-sensing and sensor data.

solution_components.name: Alibaba Cloud GPU instances
solution_components.role: Supply elastic training compute for large AI weather models and other remote-sensing workloads.

solution_components.name: Object Storage Service (OSS)
solution_components.role: Stores massive historical satellite, drone, and sensor datasets with lower-cost tiered retention.

solution_components.name: Cloud Parallel File Storage (CPFS)
solution_components.role: Provides the high-throughput, low-latency shared file access needed during AI model training.

data_flow: Satellite, drone, and sensor feeds are ingested into Dadi Quantum's spatiotemporal PaaS, where proprietary algorithms grid and organize the data pool. AI meteorology models train on that corpus using GPU instances, CPFS, and OSS, and the resulting weather and power-forecast outputs are delivered through SDK and platform services to renewable-energy and other industry users.
business_outcome: Alibaba Cloud gave Dadi Quantum an elastic foundation for commercial AI forecasting instead of forcing the company to overbuild local infrastructure. The platform can train large weather models with hundreds of CPUs and GPUs, keep vast historical datasets in lower-cost storage tiers, and deliver more precise 15-day weather and near-real-time power predictions that help renewable-energy customers improve planning, reduce grid-connection losses, and respond more confidently to electricity-market volatility.
metrics: integrates nearly 100 satellite, drone, and sensor data sources
weather forecasts cover up to 15 days
satellite data synchronizes about every 5 minutes
single training runs can use hundreds of GPUs and CPUs
architecture_clues: The implementation separates a cloud-native spatiotemporal PaaS and SDK layer from the end-to-end AI meteorology model.
CPFS and OSS are paired so model training gets low-latency reads while long-term multi-source data stays cost efficient.
Near-real-time satellite updates are fed into downstream photovoltaic and wind-power forecasting services.
The same remote-sensing foundation is reused across agriculture, energy, environmental, and geospatial products.
